instruction: Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_027_mass_target_bracket.step in SolidWorks. Using SolidWorks command-line automation, use that input file. The bracket has a 100 x 60 x 8 mm main plate and a 100 x 6 x 32 mm reinforcing rib centered on Y=0 above the plate. Without changing the outer bounding box, add four evenly distributed 6 mm diameter through lightening holes in the main plate at (X,Y)=(-30,-20), (30,-20), (-30,20), and (30,20). These holes keep the theoretical aluminum mass at density 2.70 g/cm3 within 180 +/- 2 g, pass through the main plate only, and do not cut through the reinforcing rib. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_027_mass_reduced_out.step and write C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_027_massprops.txt with the final volume and theoretical mass. [Software] Launch SOLIDWORKS from `C:\Program Files\SOLIDWORKS Corp\SOLIDWORKS\` (use your actual executable or shortcut). For this workflow, run the SOLIDWORKS automation through `C:\Program Files\SOLIDWORKS Corp\SOLIDWORKS\SLDWORKS.exe` when working on `cli_027_mass_target_bracket.step`.
